meta.what: Laundered oil per country: the value of the Russian crude inside oil products (HS 2710) that EU members imported from refiners using Russian crude (India, Turkiye, UAE, China, Singapore, Georgia), 2019-2026; plus CREA-based checks for USA, GBR, AUS.
meta.units: EUR bn, nominal; 2026 = Jan-Aug, not annualised. USD figures converted at ECB yearly averages (2023 1.081, 2024 1.082, 2025 1.13, 2026 1.16).
method: Imports: Eurostat Comext DS-045409, HS 2710, extra-EU imports by member state and country of origin, annual 2019-2025 and monthly Jan-Aug 2026 (downloaded 2026-10-18).

x Russian share of the crude in each origin's exports to the EU (low/central/high; India 0.15/0.35/0.38/0.33 in 2022-25 and 0.065 in 2026 after the 21 Jan ban; Turkiye 0.38/0.45/0.61/0.55 and 0.35; UAE 0.02-0.08; China 0.12; Singapore 0.03; Georgia Kulevi 0.8 in 2026), from CREA, CSD, Global Witness and KSE refinery data.

x k = value of Russian crude per euro of product made from it: 0.494 from CREA (EUR 4.2 bn crude for EUR 8.5 bn products, Dec 2022-Dec 2023), moved each year with Russian crude price / ULSD price: 2022 0.47, 2023 0.494, 2024 0.60, 2025 0.56, 2026 0.415, pre-war ~0.70; range x0.88-1.12.
Cyprus: imports with origin 'not specified' (QW, 0.07 bn 2021 -> 1.0 bn 2025) are counted at 40% (10-80%) from Russian-crude refiners.

Final consumer = first importer after hub pass-on with the model's own resale shares (energy2.json hub_resale central) and customers (hub_exports_2024.json) for NLD, BEL, GRC, MLT; low/high scaled by the same ratio.

Calibration checks: CREA Dec 2022-Dec 2023 EU 2.6 bn (13 months) vs 2.6 bn here for 2023; NLD 0.59 / FRA 0.42 / ITA 0.32 (13 months) vs 0.50 / 0.42 / 0.34; Global Witness 2023: 35 m bbl (~EUR 2.0-2.2 bn crude).
meta.usd_rates: ECB yearly averages as in the shared brief

BEL.role: re-exporting hub (ARA): ~48% (35-75%) resold, to NLD, NGA, DEU, FRA

CYP.role: mostly final consumer (no refinery), part bunkers; origin hidden as 'not specified' (QW) in Comext

GRC.role: partial hub: STS transfers off Laconia, bunkers and re-exports (~50% resold); also main EU destination of Turkish-port cargoes

MLT.role: bunker hub: fuel sold to passing ships; Comext shows almost no imports from these refiners

NLD.role: re-exporting hub (ARA): ~74% (60-90%) of fuel imports resold, mainly to DEU, BEL, USA, GBR, FRA

ROU.role: final consumer with transit: Constanta also forwards fuel to Moldova and Ukraine (Kpler shows more than customs)

SVN.role: partial transit: Koper port serves Austria and Hungary

USA.basis: CREA Feb 2024: EUR 807 mn Russian crude in US imports Dec 2022-Dec 2023 (13 months); CREA Feb 2026: EUR 799 mn of US imports Mar 2025-Feb 2026 made from Russian crude (product value, x0.56 crude ratio); CREA/CSD: EUR 232 mn Turkish products from Russian crude H1 2024; CREA July 2026 monthly: EUR 234 mn/month from such refineries. 2021 not estimated (pre-war base from round4a.json stays).

GBR.basis: CREA for BBC Feb 2024: GBP 569 mn (EUR ~0.655 bn) of products made from Russian crude in the 12 months after Dec 2022 (x0.494 crude ratio); S&P Global May 2026: 2025 UK imports from India ~32 kb/d jet + 7 kb/d gasoil (~EUR 1.1 bn) x 0.33 Russian share x 0.56; UK ban from 2026 exempts diesel and jet; Jamnagar jet cargo June 2026 EUR 63 mn.

AUS.basis: CREA per-country windows used in energy.json (products from Russian crude 0.86 bn 2023, 0.94 bn 2024) x crude ratio; CREA Feb 2026: Australia EUR 3.4 bn from refineries using Russian crude, EUR 1.6 bn made from Russian crude, Mar 2025-Feb 2026, incl. Brunei Hengyi (60% Russian, 98% of its sanctioning-country exports to Australia), which the model's refiner list (IN, TR, CN, AE) omits; KSE June 2026: Australia main destination of Russian-derived products in 2026.

NOR.basis: no country figure found; CREA lists Norway in G7+ but never names it among importers. Keep model.

CHE.basis: no country figure found (landlocked; imports via ARA and Rhine, so model pass-on from NLD/BEL/DEU is the right channel). Keep model.

JPN.basis: no figure found; Japan imports few products from India/Turkey. Keep model.

CAN.basis: CREA Nov 2025 lists Canada among destinations of six IN/TR refineries without a value. Keep model.

crude_content_check.model: CRUDE_CONTENT = 0.60 / 0.68 / 0.75 of product value, applied after CREA-calibrated product values
crude_content_check.evidence: CREA Feb 2024: EUR 8.5 bn products made from Russian crude used EUR 4.2 bn Russian crude -> 0.494; with prices 0.42-0.60 in 2022-2026
crude_content_check.effect: the model's crude value is ~1.2-1.6x too high for every non-EU buyer; for EU members the x0.62 Global Witness correction roughly offsets it (EU total model 7.8 bn vs 8.2 bn here, final-consumer basis 2022-2026)

overlaps: Same flow as energy.json laundered_oil and the pipeline's reassign_laundered_oil(); this file is a per-country replacement/check for EU members, not an addition. The refiner deductions (hub_buyers.json turkey_refining.double_count_at_turkey, india_refining, round4a.json china_refining) assume the exported crude is counted at buyers; if EU laundered values change, the deductions stay valid only if the global total of laundered oil stays consistent (EU change here is small: about +5% on the final-consumer basis, but large shifts between members). Direct Russian product imports (RU origin in Comext 2022-2023, Bulgaria derogation) are in to_rus, not here. Relabelled Russian products via Turkish non-refinery ports (Ceyhan, Marmara Ereglisi, Mersin; EUR 3.1-3.3 bn a year to the EU, mostly Greece) are only partly captured (Comext records many as Iraqi/Turkmen/Kazakh/Azeri origin); hub_buyers.json reexport_of_russian_products already discusses this channel and it is NOT added here. Pre-war values overlap round4a.json laundered_prewar (same concept; compare base_2019_2021).
notes: Comext records the member state where the import was declared and the origin country, so ARA hubs carry fuel later consumed elsewhere; use final_consumer values for attribution. Combining all low (or all high) factors gives ranges wider than 90%. Malta and Cyprus model values come from refiners' mirror export data (STS/bunker deliveries) that EU customs do not show.
